summary.headline: The Community Preservation Committee reviewed major Fall Town Meeting proposals, including an estimated $900,000 golf course irrigation overhaul and Fay Memorial Park upgrades.
summary.summary: The Community Preservation Committee held its annual public forum to review Community Preservation Act funding, historical town allocations, and the upcoming application cycle. The committee discussed several pending projects being prepared for the Fall Special Town Meeting, focusing heavily on a cost-engineered irrigation system for the Southborough Golf Course estimated at $900,000 and parking solutions for Fay Memorial Park. Members also reviewed standardized signage designs to recognize CPA-funded town projects and deferred voting on the updated application handbook to an upcoming meeting.

topics.title: Annual CPA public forum and program overview
topics.summary: The committee presented its annual overview of the Community Preservation Act in Southborough, covering governance, local surcharge revenues, state matches, and statutory funding allocations. Since adoption in 2003, the town has collected approximately $6.6 million locally with $2.5 million in state matches. Members outlined the minimum 10 percent statutory buckets for open space, historic preservation, and community housing, along with the September 15 application deadline for next spring's Annual Town Meeting.
key_details: Southborough voters adopted a 1 percent CPA property tax surcharge in 2003, with exemptions for qualifying seniors and low-income homeowners.
The surcharge costs the average single-family home assessed at $991,000 approximately $127.95 per year.
Total CPA funds collected to date exceed $9.1 million, including over $2.5 million from the state trust fund match.
Annual revenue is divided into open space (10 percent), historic preservation (10 percent), community housing (10 percent), administration (up to 5 percent), and budgeted reserve (65 percent).
The deadline for applications seeking funding at the 2027 Annual Town Meeting is September 15.
topics.outcome: Information presented and discussed with attendees.

topics.title: Fay Memorial Park improvements update
topics.summary: The vice chair presented an update on the Recreation Commission's proposal to repurpose Fay Memorial Park to add a dog park and a children's splash pad. Parking remains the primary neighborhood concern, and the project engineer recently delivered a traffic and parking study outlining potential layout expansions and dedicated park spaces. The Recreation Commission intends to submit a revised application by June 30 for consideration at the Fall Special Town Meeting.
key_details: Proposed park enhancements include a dog park and splash pad.
A parking study completed with engineering consultant Activitas provides options to expand and protect parking spaces for park visitors.
The Recreation Commission will coordinate with the DPW and the Select Board regarding parking utilization and agreements near the Historical Society.
The committee reiterated that revised applications for the Fall Special Town Meeting must be submitted by June 30.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; revised proposal expected by June 30.
topics.why_it_matters: The project would introduce a new dog park and water recreation amenity in town while addressing ongoing parking and traffic concerns for adjacent residents.

topics.title: Rural Cemetery stone water tower restoration
topics.summary: The Historical Commission representative provided an update on the proposed restoration of the historic stone water tower in the Rural Cemetery. Discussions remain largely stalled due to pending structural and cost consultant evaluations, as well as jurisdiction and coordination issues with the Rural Cemetery Committee. Proponents may withdraw the application from the fall warrant if alternative non-CPA solutions or independent plans proceed.
key_details: The project seeks to restore the historic stone water tower located inside the Rural Cemetery.
A consultant conducted an initial inspection and rough estimate, but a full cost report has not been completed.
Overlapping jurisdiction between the Historical Commission and the Cemetery Committee has delayed finalizing a CPA scope.
The application may be formally withdrawn if a viable submission cannot be completed.
topics.outcome: Update received; project status remains pending.

topics.title: Southborough Golf Course irrigation replacement
topics.summary: The DPW superintendent and Golf Course Committee members discussed a revised funding plan for the golf course irrigation system after initial construction bids substantially exceeded available funds. Value engineering identified approximately $160,000 in scope reductions, but engineers determined a necessary booster pump station will add roughly $200,000, bringing total project estimates to about $900,000. Proponents are reviewing how much to contribute from the golf course revolving fund, which has about $200,000 available but faces a statutory annual spending limit of $75,000 without Select Board and Advisory Committee approval.
key_details: Original construction bids came in well over the appropriated budget, triggering value engineering efforts.
Proposed cost reductions shaved roughly $160,000, but a newly required booster pump station adds approximately $200,000.
Preliminary revised total cost estimate for the irrigation project is approximately $900,000.
The golf course revolving fund has approximately $200,985 in uncommitted funds, but town policy caps annual revolving expenditures at $75,000 unless joint approval is granted.
The DPW and Golf Course Committee plan to submit a revised application and schedule by June 30, with the option to postpone to Spring Town Meeting if loose ends remain.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; revised application package due by June 30.
topics.why_it_matters: Replacing the failing irrigation system requires significant capital funding, potentially drawing hundreds of thousands of dollars from CPA reserves and municipal revolving funds.

topics.title: Peninsula Trail project update
topics.summary: The committee briefly addressed the Peninsula Trail project application. Discussion was deferred until the applicant and committee members can coordinate following a previously canceled meeting.
key_details: Project proponents will be invited to discuss the proposal at an upcoming committee meeting.
topics.outcome: Discussion continued to the next meeting.

topics.title: Standardized CPA recognition signage
topics.summary: The committee reviewed efforts to install permanent signs acknowledging CPA funding at completed projects across town. Members examined sample PVC and bronze sign mockups for the library facade, the library interior local history collection, and the golf course. Discussion centered on specific wording choices, including whether to credit 'residents', 'citizens', or 'taxpayers', and selecting standard dimensions to maintain consistency while avoiding sign clutter.
key_details: Samples presented included 12-by-16 inch PVC signs estimated at $100 each and larger versions at $150 each from Signarama.
Cast bronze signs for prominent historic structures like the library exterior and water tower range from $500 to $1,500.
The Library Trustees favored crediting the 'residents' of Southborough, while public comment urged using 'taxpayers'.
Sign mounting locations will be tailored per site, using fence mounts, posts, or building facades.
topics.outcome: Wording and final sizes will be voted on at the next meeting.

topics.title: FY27 application and handbook revisions
topics.summary: Members discussed updating the annual CPA application form and informational handbook. The committee agreed to provide editable Word document versions in addition to PDFs to avoid past issues with fillable forms, and agreed to review text changes and updated deadlines at the next meeting.
key_details: The committee will provide application forms in Microsoft Word format to simplify applicant submissions.
Updated dates and application instructions will be reviewed and finalized at the next session.
topics.outcome: Handbook review deferred to the next meeting.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved past meeting minutes and discussed scheduling its next meeting before the end of June. The meeting was adjourned at approximately 9:09 p.m.
key_details: Approved meeting minutes from February 26, 2026 and May 20, 2026.
Members agreed to poll dates for the next meeting prior to June 30.
topics.outcome: Minutes approved; next meeting date to be scheduled via poll.

public_comment.summary: The chair of the Master Plan Implementation Committee, speaking as a resident, asked how the Community Preservation Committee could collaborate to proactively advance priorities and recommendations identified in the town master plan.
A resident of 1 Chestnut Hill Road inquired about the requirements, historic restrictions, and Massachusetts anti-aid amendment rules governing CPA funding for private historic structures.

A resident of Woodbury Road recommended using the word 'taxpayers' rather than 'citizens' or 'residents' on CPA signs, noting that many property and business taxpayers contributing to the fund are non-residents.
